exactGap: Named modes do not exist as a product concept: only PermissionMode Auto/Ask/Deny (execution-core permission/mod.rs:6-20, whose from_wire maps any unknown string to Auto), a server-floored ApprovalPosture per profile (model-gateway profile.rs:95-125) and a plan-approval AutonomyRung grant (mp-contracts autonomy.rs:45-59, ChatMessages.tsx:2536-2542) exist, with no per-thread or Space persistence and no org cap. The hook engine is real (execution-core hook/mod.rs:113) but HookRegistry is in-memory (runtime_registries.rs:2003), RegisterHook has no gateway or UI caller (grpc.rs:2052), hook_context reaches only browser runs and the chat code_interpreter call (browser_run.rs:418, tools.rs:211) while the Do loop passes an empty string (agent.rs:1927); a durable hook_configs table already exists in session-core (migration 0004:165) but nothing reads or writes it except GDPR erasure. There is no org policy registry, setting lock, lockdown profile, frozen tool snapshot or unified Customize hub; a per-server exact-name MCP tool_allowlist (fail-closed) and admin Settings sections for MCP servers, plugins, skills and org instructions do exist, but tool schemas are re-discovered live (runtime_registries.rs:797) and plugin manifests are inert.
reuse: AutonomyRung ladder, strictly-wider escalation and per-call permits() check (mp-contracts autonomy.rs)

Existing Settings sections (mcp, skills, plugins, org-instructions, persona, integrations) as the hub backbone
Control-signed decision key distribution (CONTROL_SPACE_DECISION_KEY_ID / public key env) for signed policy bundles
constraints: Control Plane owns org identity and policy, so the registry and its signing belong there; Model Plane only enforces and must verify signed bundles (no cross-plane DB reads). Policy may only tighten: copy the resolve_posture rule that a client request can raise strictness but never fall below the server floor. Owner-plane effects are never auto-approved (permission/mod.rs:53-58), so a "full access" mode cannot lower that durable-approval requirement. PermissionMode::from_wire currently fails open to Auto for unknown strings, so new modes must not ride that parser until it fails closed. ZDR turns run a persistence-free path that already refuses tool lists and plan mode (model-gateway zdr_features.rs), so modes and hooks have nothing to govern there and lockdown must not become a ZDR bypass. Org policy must never widen Space access.
approachAdjustment: The item bundles seven independent workstreams across three planes; split it. (1) Plan B4 (S): pass hook_context into the Do loop (agent.rs:1927 passes an empty string). (2) Durable hooks: do not invent a table; session-core hook_configs already has the schema, so decide owner (session-core vs capability-core per CR-04), add an admin API and a gateway/UI caller. (3) AgentMode: map each named mode onto the existing PermissionMode plus AutonomyRung server-side, clamped by an org cap. (4) Org policy registry, locks and lockdown: Control Plane, signed, tighten-only, with a fail-closed value per key. (5) Frozen tool snapshots: pin tool name plus description hash plus schema hash at admin approval (today only names are allow-listed). (6) Hub: extend the existing Settings sections; the premise that admins have no product surface is wrong for MCP, plugins, skills and org instructions, and the real gap is hooks, modes and locks. Also correct "hooks only reach browser runs": they also reach the chat code_interpreter call.
effortNote: As one item this spans Control (registry, signing), Model Plane (clamp, hooks, snapshots) and Frontend (hub, mode picker), so L understates it. Split as S (Do-run hook_context, already plan B4), M (durable hooks plus admin API), M (AgentMode), L (policy registry, locks, lockdown), M (hub and frozen snapshots).
verdictReason: The enforcement core and several admin surfaces already exist, so the item must stop implying an empty product surface and must be split; the true gaps are named modes, durable hooks wired to Do runs, org locks and lockdown, snapshot pinning and a unified hub.

constraints: Control owns the retention policy and legal hold (identity/orgs/audit); session-core sweeps only its own rows and must propagate to Data Plane indexes and Letta memory through events and receipts, never by cross-plane DB access (gdpr.rs itself notes cost-core is unreachable). A legal hold must outrank the sweeper but interacts with GDPR erasure (Space deletion already has a blocked_legal_hold status), so precedence needs a Control decision. ZDR runs persist no content, so a hold cannot apply to them and the sweeper has nothing to delete; return a typed refusal rather than silence. Share links are authority-bearing: Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL, ZDR threads must be refused, and the grant belongs in Control rather than only in session-core.
approachAdjustment: Place the share-link grant in Control (issue and verify, like Space read decisions) with session-core enforcing it, instead of designing it in session-core alone. Reuse the existing Space legal-hold contract rather than adding a new flag shape, and either wire or delete the unused org-core Compliance struct (DataRetentionDays, HIPAACompliant) so there is one retention field. Split the item into independent workstreams: retention window plus org/thread hold with dry-run and audit (L), data-use label (S), regime tags (M), share-link ADR then build (L), typed telemetry registry (M), and release pipeline (M: invoke release-artifact.sh from CI, pin actions by SHA, add cargo-audit/cargo-deny and govulncheck to the Model Plane workflows). Do not claim signed releases until a candidate with rollback has actually been built.
effortNote: Six sub-workstreams across Control, Model Plane and Support Plane; sequence retention and hold first. Individually S to L.
verdictReason: Several pieces already exist (Space legal hold, audit retention sweeper, privacy tiers, temporary chat, release-artifact tooling), so the item should be reworded to say exactly which parts are missing and split so retention/hold, share links and the release pipeline can ship independently.

The only substrate is the HTML artifact preview: ArtifactHtmlPreview renders srcdoc with sandbox="allow-scripts" and no allow-same-origin under a CSP of default-src none, connect-src none and inline scripts only (ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:512-523, sandbox-html.ts:10-30); no postMessage handler or dedicated origin exists. constraints: Every app-initiated tools/call must pass the capability gate and org MCP allow-list and be attributed to the viewing user, never the artifact author. ZDR: no artifact persistence and no viewer key-value store under ZDR. A new user-content origin is a new attack surface and needs an ADR. The MCP client currently opens one short session per call, so server-initiated elicitation must be handled inside the tools/call SSE stream and routed into the existing human-approval pause. The preview CSP blocks remote scripts and connections, so a per-app CSP from declared metadata would have to be built and org-restricted.
approachAdjustment: Do not make the dedicated user-content origin a prerequisite. The existing opaque-origin srcdoc frame can host a postMessage bridge that authenticates by event.source equal to iframe.contentWindow; a separate-origin frame shell is needed only if apps require same-origin web APIs, SRI-loaded libraries or shareable URLs, which is an ADR decision (inference, medium confidence). Merge the artifact host bridge with F-t3-044 and split elicitation (MCP client plus HITL card, smaller) from MCP Apps. The dependency note that F-t3-003 "makes MCP callable" is inaccurate: MCP tools are already callable through mcp_call; F-t3-003 supplies side-effect classes and the signed gate.
effortNote: Holds for elicitation plus MCP Apps on the existing sandboxed frame; the dedicated origin, viewer-bound connectors and viewer key-value store push it to XL and should be a separate later item.
verdictReason: The capability is genuinely absent, but the dedicated origin is not required for a first bridge and the bridge overlaps F-t3-044; reword to MCP elicitation and MCP Apps on the existing sandbox, with origin and viewer storage deferred.

constraints: Model proposes and Quarry executes, so any recording is a Quarry-side artifact and the proof bundle carries only a reference, never bytes (events deliberately exclude extracted_text, browser_events.rs:192-200). ZDR: Quarry declines to persist artifacts on ZDR runs (AgentRunConsole.tsx:2054-2062), so no clip exists under ZDR by construction. approachAdjustment: Add playback and a slider to the existing BrowserChrome timeline (already reused in the chat panel) and surface the same rationale in the Run Console; do not build a second timeline. For the walkthrough, consider assembling a low-rate clip or filmstrip from the per-step screenshots Quarry already stores before building continuous 12 fps video capture (inference): it needs no new capture and is ZDR-safe by construction. Attach the resulting artifact reference to the proof bundle as a new section.
effortNote: Unchanged for scrubber plus a screenshot-assembled clip (the scrubber alone is S and a quick win); true continuous video recording in Quarry would be L.
verdictReason: The event data, step timeline, rationale and screenshots already exist, so the item should read as playback controls plus a clip over existing evidence rather than a new replay system.
